A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between pages and appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original routing experiments on RouterBench and SPROUT, including utility, accuracy–cost curves, and results across ten trials.

after.justification: The original benchmark experiments remain, and Appendix D additionally reports a routing-latency measurement.

M1.justification: The counterfactual estimator, classification and softmax training approaches, interval-conditioned architecture, and deployment procedure remain unchanged. The revised classification bound changes theoretical justification without establishing a change to the implemented loss or routing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RouterBench and SPROUT with the same task coverage and fixed versus held-out cost-preference scenarios. The new latency example reuses RouterBench.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain Full-Feedback, Baseline, R&C, Causal-CARROT with kNN and EmbedNet, and CF-Regression. No evaluated routing comparator is added, removed, or substantively revised.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a latency evaluation using Llama-3.2-1B embeddings and an MLP router on one A100 GPU with a batch of almost 25,000. The existing utility experiments retain their splits, observational sampling, cost-preference grids, and training settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a limited computational-efficiency analysis assessing routing overhead through a latency example and comparison with generation times. New Appendix C interprets existing method comparisons; it does not introduce controlled component ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: The ten-trial protocol and existing mean-plus/minus and average-AUC reporting remain unchanged. The added latency result introduces no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimate, or significance test.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–7 and accuracy–cost plots are unchanged. The later version adds latency below 2.5 ms and Appendix C's stated accuracy-gain ranges of 10–15%, 1–3%, and 0.5–1% from the retained comparisons, without new supporting tables.

T1.justification: Definition 1 and revised Proposition 1 replace the discrete-action Lipschitz assumption and distance bound with a probability-simplex formulation and a square-root cross-entropy bound for stochastic policies. Appendix A adds a Pinsker-inequality derivation, substantially revising the classification surrogate's theoretical support. Propositions 2–5 remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same main contributions: causal routing from observational data, two regret surrogates, heterogeneous cost preferences, and superior benchmark performance.

C2.justification: New Remark 1 explicitly describes the framework as estimator-agnostic. Appendix C strengthens component-level interpretations, including claiming Baseline performs worst across all settings, while Appendix D newly argues that routing overhead is negligible. These extend the discussion without changing the main contribution claims.

D1.justification: The experimental details formerly in Appendix C are retained in Appendix D. The latency paragraph adds hardware and batch-size information for that measurement; existing software, training hyperparameters, preprocessing, embedding generation, and propensity-model details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, as is the substantive positioning relative to prior predictive routing, CARROT, and causal policy learning. The new discussion reuses those existing relationships.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting accompanies the revised classification argument, new estimator remark, component-discussion appendix, and latency paragraph. Experimental Details moves from Appendix C to D, with small wording and conference-footer edits elsewhere; the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: All six figures and seven tables are retained without redesigned content. Their placement changes: Figure 2 moves to page 9, appendix figures redistribute, and Tables 3–6 are grouped on page 17 in v2.

improvement.justification: The revised simplex formulation and Pinsker proof provide an explicit connection between cross-entropy and estimated stochastic regret that v1 lacked, yielding a localized theoretical improvement. Benchmark evidence remains unchanged. Benefits are tempered by Appendix C's overstated rankings: its claim that Baseline is always worst conflicts with Table 2 at lambda=500, where Baseline scores 54.08 versus Causal-CARROT (EmbedNet)'s 48.91. The new latency comparison also leaves embedding-computation costs unclear.
